svg.title: $550,000 Revenue to $206,250 Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-commission-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $550,000 Revenue to $206,250 Owner Net; subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to the 37.5% Base-Case margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: USD annually. Opening revenue and closing profit are absolute total bars; the four intervening bars are signed deductions. The expense allocation is editorial, while scenario totals are canonical. Conservative: $100,000 revenue, 25% margin, $25,000 owner net, 1 FT + 3 C. Base: $550,000 revenue, 37.5% margin, $206,250 owner net, 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled: $1,000,000 revenue, 50% margin, $500,000 owner net, 2 FT + 4 C.; caption: $550,000 - $150,000 - $108,000 - $60,000 - $25,750 = $206,250. Total expenses are $343,750, or 62.5% of retained commissions. Owner net is modeled before personal income taxes; owner draws are not a second expense.; stages: label: Retained commission revenue; value: $550,000 earned from ten completed commission events.; numeric value: 550000.0; detail: Opening total equals ten closings multiplied by $55,000 retained commission. Outside-broker shares are excluded before this revenue basis is measured; escrow principal and asset purchase prices never enter it.; label: Deal-specific delivery costs; value: Deduct $150,000 for externally purchased transaction support.; numeric value: -150000.0; detail: Budget $15,000 per closing-equivalent for specialist inspection, transaction support, travel, and diligence. The annual allocation includes work on failed deals. Vendors are purchased services, not additional pod seats.; label: Three contractor seats; value: Deduct $108,000 across three defined contractor scopes.; numeric value: -108000.0; detail: Allocate $36,000 annually to each core contractor scope: research, documents, and transaction coordination. These are budgeted service scopes rather than three full-time employee salaries; classification follows actual work arrangements.; label: Core operating overhead; value: Deduct $60,000 for systems, prospecting, and administration.; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Allocate $5,000 monthly to CRM, secure document storage, sector data, prospecting, bookkeeping, and administration. Combined with $9,000 monthly contractor spend, recurring modeled overhead is $14,000 monthly.; label: Insurance and dispute expense; value: Deduct $25,750 for coverage and modeled dispute costs.; numeric value: -25750.0; detail: Include transaction-services coverage, deductibles, and dispute-resolution costs as annual modeled expenses. This line is not an escrow balance or a cash reserve transfer. Avoid duplicating deal-specific delivery costs.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $206,250 remains after all four modeled expense categories.; numeric value: 206250.0; detail: Closing total equals $550,000 multiplied by 37.5%. The full-time principal receives the residual owner economics; no separate principal salary is deducted in this illustrative owner-operated expense bridge.

rect.title: label: Retained commission revenue; value: $550,000 earned from ten completed commission events.; numeric value: 550000.0; detail: Opening total equals ten closings multiplied by $55,000 retained commission. Outside-broker shares are excluded before this revenue basis is measured; escrow principal and asset purchase prices never enter it.

label: Deal-specific delivery costs; value: Deduct $150,000 for externally purchased transaction support.; numeric value: -150000.0; detail: Budget $15,000 per closing-equivalent for specialist inspection, transaction support, travel, and diligence. The annual allocation includes work on failed deals. Vendors are purchased services, not additional pod seats.

label: Three contractor seats; value: Deduct $108,000 across three defined contractor scopes.; numeric value: -108000.0; detail: Allocate $36,000 annually to each core contractor scope: research, documents, and transaction coordination. These are budgeted service scopes rather than three full-time employee salaries; classification follows actual work arrangements.

label: Core operating overhead; value: Deduct $60,000 for systems, prospecting, and administration.; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Allocate $5,000 monthly to CRM, secure document storage, sector data, prospecting, bookkeeping, and administration. Combined with $9,000 monthly contractor spend, recurring modeled overhead is $14,000 monthly.

label: Insurance and dispute expense; value: Deduct $25,750 for coverage and modeled dispute costs.; numeric value: -25750.0; detail: Include transaction-services coverage, deductibles, and dispute-resolution costs as annual modeled expenses. This line is not an escrow balance or a cash reserve transfer. Avoid duplicating deal-specific delivery costs.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $206,250 remains after all four modeled expense categories.; numeric value: 206250.0; detail: Closing total equals $550,000 multiplied by 37.5%. The full-time principal receives the residual owner economics; no separate principal salary is deducted in this illustrative owner-operated expense bridge.
